rv.q: Majok, a Tony nominee and Pulitzer Prize-winner for her play “Cost of Living,” skillfully weaves together the women’s experiences of desperation, grief and survival.
"Queens," directed with a sensitive hand by Trip Cullman, is more loosely constructed (and prolix) than some of Ms. Majok’s plays, reflecting the scattered nature of its characters’ experiences.
These interludes are powerful, but so stylistically different from the rest of the play as to feel jarring.
And yet, as strong as its message is, and as well acted, there are structural problems with the play that undermine its full power.
This specific production of 'queens' is not to be missed.
Martyna Majok’s Queens turns a cramped Queens basement into a stage for American ambition, powered by Marin Ireland and an ensemble that refuses to beg for your pity.

cn.t: Majok's bleak but moving drama about undocumented women in a Queens basement earns praise for powerful performances and timely relevance, though some find the nearly three-hour runtime excessive.
